messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Alert: dedpool node failure detected in pool dedpool-echonova-3. Cause: PCIe AER errors, GPU 0 kernel panic. Active tenants: ech-3421 (Echonova Therapeutics). Impact: affected jobs are being evicted/failing. Pager severity: P1.
Alex (oncall-sre): Acknowledged. Oncall here. Kicking off runbook: dedpool-drain-and-replace v2. Jamie you're handoff if I need to go offline.
Jamie (sre-rotation): I'm available. What's the immediate customer impact?
Alex (oncall-sre): ech-3421 has ~12 active inferences, latency spikes and 502 errors. CS pinged. Need isolation -> drain node, failover tenant to fallback reserved capacity or route to compatible hosted model.
Maya (customer-success): I just pinged their security lead and infra contact. They see increased error rate. Asked for ETA and mitigation plan.
Lee (eng-runtime): Recommending live drain + route policy to fallback model variant (quant-8bit-compatible) to keep requests flowing. We'll accept slight quality variance.
Ravi (infra): Hardware call: looks like persistent PCIe AER on GPU0, board-level fault. Spare on-site replacement available but needs swap (approx 45m ETA). We can hot-replace if we evacuate jobs.
Alex (oncall-sre): Steps I'm running now: 1) mark node draining 2) set policy to route ech-3421 to fallback pool in parallel 3) snapshot active KV caches for warm restart.
Alex (oncall-sre): Running commands:
```
# mark node draining
redwoodctl pool drain --pool dedpool-echonova-3 --node gpu-node-77 --reason "PCIe AER kernel panic"
# route policy update
redwoodctl route update --tenant ech-3421 --fallback-pool reserved-eu-west-2-small --timeout 30s
# snapshot KV
redwoodctl kv snapshot --pool dedpool-echonova-3 --node gpu-node-77 --out /tmp/kv-snap-201800
```
Jamie (sre-rotation): Saw the drain call go through. Node is rejecting new allocations. Eviction started. Current evict log: 6/12 sessions migrated, 3 retrying, 3 in-progress.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary routing change applied to 30% of ech-3421 traffic. Logs: route-update: OK.
Lee (eng-runtime): Adding runtime tweak — reduce batch size for fallback model to keep latency under SLO. Patch config: `max_batch_tokens: 512 -> 256` for reserved-eu-west-2-small.
Maya (customer-success): Echonova asking about data residency — confirm fallback pool is in eu-west and in their VPC tenant. I told them yes and initiated a support ticket (INC-2026-4821).
Ravi (infra): Hot-swap prep: techs onsite cleared. Spare board pre-staged. ETA now 33m. If we can't replace in 45m, plan to migrate workloads to temporaries and consider adding burst capacity from dedicated spare fleet.
Alex (oncall-sre): Risk note: if we route to hosted models, some requests might see model variant mismatch. Documenting mitigation for SLO/regression. Creating smoky regression watch.
Jamie (sre-rotation): Progress update 18m in: eviction complete for first 9 sessions. Two long-running evals still stuck; contacting owners to abort or checkpoint.
Lee (eng-runtime): Pushing automated KV restore on destination pool to warm caches for migrated sessions: `redwoodctl kv restore --from /tmp/kv-snap-201800 --to reserved-eu-west-2-small`
Alex (oncall-sre): Customer-facing message drafted: "We're seeing a hardware fault on a node in your dedicated pool. We've drained the node, routed traffic to a reserved fallback in your region, and are replacing the failed hardware. Expect normal service in ~40 min; we'll update sooner if ETA changes." Maya to send?
Maya (customer-success): Sending now. I'll include INC-2026-4821 and provide the live link to fallback metrics.
ops-bot: Incident note appended to ticket INC-2026-4821: "drain initiated, fallback routing applied, hardware replacement ETA 33m"
Alex (oncall-sre): Monitoring. If replacement completes, we'll return capacity and reverse-route after health checks. Postmortem owner: Alex + Ravi.
Jamie (sre-rotation): Any follow-up actions for infra pre-PO? Recommend firmware check on NIC and PCIe lanes, and to schedule predictive disk/GPU diagnostics for full pool.
Ravi (infra): Will run full diagnostics during replacement. Filing a hardware RMA if any nontrivial failure persists.
Lee (eng-runtime): After stable, recommend a short canary period: route 10% back for 15m and run regression prompts. Adding alert to quality monitoring.
Alex (oncall-sre): Update 28m: replacement tech confirms swap started. Node coming back offline for provisioning. I'll coordinate final health checks.
Maya (customer-success): Customer acknowledged, appreciated the quick updates. They asked for a follow-up postmortem and RCA.
Alex (oncall-sre): Closing loop plan: 1) confirm node healthy 2) reverse-route 3) monitor 30m 4) postmortem + RCA + customer summary. Will keep thread live until full return.
ops-bot: Automated health-check: gpu-node-77 -> status: provisioning, gpu0 still shows ECC > threshold, re-running burn-in.
Jamie (sre-rotation): Noted. If ECC persists, we'll keep node out of rotation and spin up replacement instance.
Alex (oncall-sre): Last update before handoff: replacement in finalization, all migrated sessions stable on fallback, errors down to baseline. Handing to Jamie for overnight watch and postmortem.
Jamie (sre-rotation): Taking. Posting incident timeline to the incident tracker and assigning tasks: RCA (Alex/Ravi), customer summary (Maya), infra action (Ravi).
ops-bot: Incident closed? No — will remain open until postmortem created.
Alex (oncall-sre): Thanks team.
Maya (customer-success): Thanks all :thumbsup:
Lee (eng-runtime): Good job everyone.
Ravi (infra): Copy. Will follow up on hardware RMA details.
